html:
The Occohannock were an Algonquian people of the Eastern Shore of Virginia, on the peninsula between Chesapeake Bay and the Atlantic. With the Accomack to the south they formed a small chiefdom under a leader the English called the "Laughing King", Debedeavon.

They stood on the edge of the realm of Powhatan across the bay and kept a looser tie to it. When the English arrived at Jamestown in 1607 the Eastern Shore peoples traded corn with them and stayed mostly at peace. English settlers moved onto the shore from the 1620s, and over the next century the Occohannock lost their land and merged with neighbours such as the Nanticoke.
